dedupe_keys.name: sup3r spatiotemporal climate and energy resource downscaling

description: Sup3r is national laboratory software for producing fine-scale climate and energy-resource inputs from coarse data. It trains generative adversarial networks using high-resolution historical information, then applies them to reanalysis or climate-model fields. The Python data handler reads HDF5 and NetCDF, while examples and a command-line interface support training, inference and HPC execution. Documented applications span 0.5–4-kilometre grids and 5–60-minute time intervals, depending on the model. Geographic extent and time horizon remain application-specific. Source and installation instructions are publicly available free under BSD-3-Clause; training data and generated datasets are separate resources with their own provenance. A material distinction is that Sup3rCC climate scenarios do not reconstruct historical weather events, whereas the Sup3rWind application downscales historical reanalysis. Learned fine-scale structure must therefore be assessed for each application, not treated as measured local weather. Outputs support renewable-generation and climate-resilience simulations, including energy-system studies using PyPSA (model-pypsa). The existing Sup3rLoad dataset record is a distinct product, not coverage of this general downscaling software.
